full_judgment:
2. The opposite party No.1 as pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous case being No.53 of 2007 on 15.8.2007 under section 96(1) (III) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Dinajpur against the petitioner and others opposite parties for pre-emption. 

 6. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that both the Courts below without applying their judicial mind and without considering the facts and circumstances and specially the provisions of law most illegally and in an arbitrary manner rejected the application thereby the Courts below committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice. He submits that the application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure in a miscellaneous proceeding is very much maintainable in view of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention the learned Advocate referred the decisions reported in 13 BLD (1993) (AD) 57. By placing the Act 34 of 2006 he submits that the aforesaid provisions of law came into force with effect from 20.9.2006 and from than a contiguous land owner cannot invoke the provision of section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption and in the case in hand since the transfer is after promulgation of the aforesaid Act, the miscellaneous proceeding is hopelessly barred by law and thus attract the provision of order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the miscellaneous case is liable to be rejected. The learned Advocate by referring section 60 of the Registration Act submits that in numerous decision this Court as well as our Apex Court came to a conclusion that for the purpose pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act transfer means transfer as per section 60 of the Registration Act not the date on which the sale deed was executed. In support of his contention the learned Advocate referred the decisions reported in 42 DLR (AD) 123, and 3 BLT (1995) (AD) 134. He further submits that there is no ambiguity in the present case in hand and as such on the question of law the miscellaneous case can be rejected which is apparent on the face on record i.e. Act 34 of 2006. In support of his contention the learned Advocate referred a decision reported in 1 ADC 254. Regarding the question of maintainability of the appeal as raised by the learned Advocate for the opposite party. He submits that there is a Specific provision for preferring appeal and in view of the specific provision in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the petitioner preferred appeal otherwise the petitioner would have preferred the procedure laid down in section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 9. In numerous cases this Court as well as our Apex Court came to a conclusion that the provisions laid down in the Code of Civil procedure is very much applicable in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950. In the case reported in 13 BLD (AD) 57 their Lordships held; 

 10. In view of the aforesaid decisions it appears that an application under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure can be maintained in a miscellaneous proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act since the proceeding is a miscellaneous one. 

 11. In the case in hand it appears that the pre-emptor instituted the case on 15.8.2007 and the alleged kabula was executed on 24.11.2005. It appears that the legislature amended the provision laid down in section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act with effect from 20.9.2006 vide Act 34 of 2006. By the said amendment the legislatures debarred a contiguous land owner from invoking the right of pre-emption. In the case in hand the pre-emptor opposite party No.1 invokes under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as contiguous land owner. 

 12. Section 96(18) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 (as - amended) by Act 34 of 2006 runs as follows; 

 "Nothing in this section shall apply to any transfer of any portion or share of a holding of a raiyat or any application under section 96 of this Act, made prior to coming into force of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 2006." 

 15. Section 60 of the Registration Act deals with the provisions regarding issuance of certificate. The question of transfer in a miscellaneous proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act raised time and again and this Court as well as of our Apex Court came to a conclusion that the transfer in the case of pre-emption is the transfer as per section 60 of the Registration Act, not the date of the execution of the sale deed. 

 "Dr. Ahmed Husain, learned Advocate for the petitioner has urged before us the ground of limitation only. He has questioned the view of the High Court Division that for the purpose of preemption the date of transfer will be the date of registration of the kabala, whereas under section 47 of the Registration Act, a transfer takes effect from the date of execution of the kabala. This is a question which has been long settled by a series of decisions to the effect that transfer within the meaning of section 96 of the state Acquisition Act, is completed when a certificate is issued by the registering officer that the document has been registered. Registration is a process which is completed on the dated this certificate is issued. This has nothing to do with the date from which the transfer takes effect. For the purpose of filing an application for pre-emption, it is the date of registration which is of material importance. The next question urged by the leaned Advocate is that in this case the respondents knew of the transfer long before the date of registration, and as such limitation will start form the date of this knowledge. There is hardly any substance in this argument for, the right to preemption accrues on the date the kabala is registered, and from this date, the application for preemption in this case was filed within the prescribed time." 

 20. So it appears that the transfer for the purpose of pre-emption is not the transfer by execution of sale deed but the transfer as per section 60 of the Registration Act which is admittedly in the case in hand after promulgation of Act 34 of 2006. Since before Registration of deed of sale under section 60 of the Registration Act the law came into operation as such the pre-emptor in the case in hand is barred by the said Act 34 of 2006 claiming the right of pre-emption as a contiguous land owner. Admittedly as per the decision reported in 1 ADC 254 in there is any doubt or allegation regarding the nature of transaction the Court requires to examined the case on merit and admittedly there is no scope to go beyond the plaint while dealing in an application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code. But in the case in hand it is apparent on the face of the new law namely the amended under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act that the pre-emption case is hopelessly barred by law. The Courts below ought to have considered this aspect by applying their judicial mind and by interpreting the law in its true perspective. 

 21. Regarding the question of revision or appeal it appears that all the procedure of the Code of Civil Procedure is to be followed in any proceeding in the absence of any specific provision. But on perusal of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it appears that the same contained a specific provisions for filing of appeal and as such the petitioner committed no illegality in filing the appeal before the lower appellate Court below.
